pr_body:
This contains 2 fixes affecting SSL_key_update():

- Don't reset the packet pointer in ssl3_setup_read_buffer

Sometimes this function gets called when the buffers have already been
set up. If there is already a partial packet in the read buffer then the
packet pointer will be set to an incorrect value. The packet pointer already
gets reset to the correct value when we first read a packet anyway, so we
don't also need to do it in ssl3_setup_read_buffer.

- Disallow SSL_key_update() if there are writes pending

If an application is halfway through writing application data it should
not be allowed to attempt an SSL_key_update() operation. Instead the
SSL_write() operation should be completed.

The former issue can result in a "bad record mac" problem if a partial record read occurs around the same time as a key update.

Fixes #13729
Fixes #12485

PR #16021 will provide tests for these scenarios.

This should also be applied to 1.1.1, but I will wait until this is approved to create a PR there since it requires some minor adjustment there.

issue_context.title: 1.1.1f： If call SSL_key_update while writes are pending（no-blocking socket），next SSL_write or SSL_read will return fail
comments: Isn't this a duplicate of #12411 ?

> Isn't this a duplicate of #12411 ?

YES，issue 12411 no one responded. I cannot guarantee that this is a bug or a usage problem。 so I submit a issue:question

It's probably going to be either me or @mattcaswell responding -- Matt was on holiday last week and my attention was focused elsewhere by a big deadline.  I intend to look at it "soon" but cannot commit to having the time available quite yet.

@kaduk @mattcaswell 
Can you pay attention to this issue?

It turns out that this is a fair bit easier to understand from the `SSL_key_update()` side than the state-machine side.
Namely, we only check `!SSL_is_init_finished()` before forcibly setting "in init" via `ossl_statem_set_in_init()`.
Presumably we need to be adding some kind of check against `rlayer.wpend_tot` to `SSL_key_update()` (the simplest thing would be to just deny the request to do a key update if writes are still pending, though if that was too disruptive we could add another flag bit and check it later).
@mattcaswell does the simple approach (return an error from `SSL_key_update()` if writes are pending) seem okay to you?

> @mattcaswell does the simple approach (return an error from SSL_key_update() if writes are pending) seem okay to you?

This seems like a reasonable approach. We better just be sure to update the documentation to make sure we capture this restriction.

> You confirm that this is not an interface usage logic problem.
Have you confirmed that this is a bug now? Do you plan to implement changes in later versions?

Yes, it looks like a bug. I'm hoping @kaduk is going to come up with a fix :-)
I have a todo item, yes.  This week is busy for me, though, so no ETA

> You confirm that this is not an interface usage logic problem.
Have you confirmed that this is a bug now? 

I'd follow-up on Matt's answer to say that this actually is an application's interface-usage logic problem, but that there's a bug in that the library should return an error gracefully in this situation and not corrupt the state of the SSL object.  The application will still need to change its code to not attempt to call `SSL_key_update()` while writes are pending.

@kaduk @mattcaswell   
When ```SSL_key_update()``` is called during non-blocking read, can the same problem  appear？

I expect so, yes.
The sketch of a patch I have in mind will cover that case, too.

Having looked at this a bit, it may actually be pretty easy to get the more-preferred functionality where we allow the API call at any time and defer the write until it is safe to do so.  The code change itself might look like https://github.com/kaduk/openssl/commit/b653b50aca4fd6e75048b9929b2d067849343aaa but it needs tests and maybe docs before it's ready to become a PR.  It might be useful to have specific tests for when a local keyupdate request is triggered but a peer's update request comes in before the locally-triggered one is written.

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/3094351625f0b222f92c22ce4943461df8c7e301/ssl/s3_lib.c#L4582-L4604
@kaduk 
1. The preceding modification only does not update the key when the Complete record is not written. However, the same problem occurs when the Complete record is not read. Therefore, check like  lines 4587 and 4588.

2. The key status is successfully updated, but the key update is not triggered. I think the new check interface is more reasonable. The new interface (```ssl_keyupdate_check```) helps users understand why the key is not updated.

TLS 1.2 renegotiation has different semantics than the TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate -- renegotiation is in some sense a synchronization point at which both read and write keys are changed, whereas the KeyUpdate is a unilateral "I am changing my keys now" message.  You can request the other party to do the same, but that happens asynchronously.  So I don't think that KeyUpdate needs to depend on having read a complete record.

@yangyangtiantianlonglong  I don't understand what you mean in your (2) -- which "key status" is updated, and when?  What is the "key update" that is not triggered?  I think I understand that you are proposing a new (perhaps `static_inline`) API called `ssl_keyupdate_check()` to encapsulate the needed logic for whether it is safe to do a key update ... but do you mean just the TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate or is it supposed to be of broader applicability?

https://github.com/kaduk/openssl/commit/b653b50aca4fd6e75048b9929b2d067849343aaa
(2)```RECORD_LAYER_write_pending```  return 1, ```SSL_key_update``` return 1, The next step does not send the keyupdate msg.
However, the users believes that the update has been successful；Because ```SSL_key_update``` is successful.

SSL_key_update will set to keyupdate  with handshake state，and will reset the record buf， How this design consider? Will it possible change to finish the current read record buffer before send the keyupdate?
